WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go." Exodus 5:2
Exodus says that Pharaoh hardened his heart, and that the LORD hardened it, as the LORD had told Moses beforehand. Exodus 4:21 Exodus 8:15 Exodus 8:32 Exodus 9:12 Exodus 9:34 Exodus 10:20 +1 more
After the hail he said, "I have sinned this time: the LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked". Exodus 9:27
At midnight of the last plague he called for Moses and Aaron: "Rise up, and get you forth from among my people ... and bless me also." Exodus 12:31–32
The LORD said to him, "for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power", words Paul quotes in Romans. Exodus 9:16 Romans 9:17
The psalm: the LORD "overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea". Psalms 136:15
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Moses asked to go "three days' journey into the wilderness" to sacrifice, since Israel's sacrifices would be "the abomination of the Egyptians". Exodus 8:25–28
The magicians copied the first signs, then said, "This is the finger of God". Exodus 7:11 Exodus 8:7 Exodus 8:18–19
Israel's officers were beaten when the tale of bricks was not met without straw. Exodus 5:14–16
Pharaoh's own servants said, "let the men go ... knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?" Exodus 10:7
Israel's officers told Moses and Aaron they had made Israel's savour "to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh". Exodus 5:20–21
The Egyptians gave Israel jewels of silver and gold and raiment as they left. Exodus 12:35–36

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given

No name and no years. 1 Kings 6:1 dates the start of Solomon's temple to "the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt"; how that is turned into a BC year, and which king it gives, are the views below.
Amenophis, son of Rameses Miamun
James Ussher (1658)
Ussher, following Manetho's list of kings, makes the king of the Exodus Amenophis, son and successor of Rameses Miamun: "he that was drowned in the red Sea".[64]
In Egypt's 18th dynasty, counted from 1 Kings 6:1
Edward Mack (1915); C. R. Conder (1915)

Mack counts the 480 years of 1 Kings 6:1 back from the founding of Solomon's temple (969 or 970 BC on his reckoning) and reaches "approximately 1448 BC". Conder takes the 480 years to run from Joshua's conquest, adds the forty years in the wilderness, puts the Exodus about 1520 BC, and makes its Pharaoh Amenophis II or Thothmes IV. 1 Kings 6:1 [11][10]
Late in the 18th dynasty, under Amenophis III
J. Lieblein, as reported by C. R. Conder (1915)
Conder reports that Lieblein placed the Exodus "late in the time of Amenophis III".[10]
Under Merenptah, successor of Rameses II
R. Lepsius (1840s), as reported by C. R. Conder; S. R. Driver (1911); W. M. F. Petrie (1915)

Raamses (Exod 1:11) takes its name from Rameses II, who founded Pithom; Exodus 2:23 and 4:19 suggest the king of the Exodus was the oppressor's successor, Merenptah. Lepsius, as Conder reports, put the Exodus in 1314 BC, Merenptah's fifteenth year; Driver gives Merenptah 1234–1214 BC on Petrie's dates; Petrie puts the Exodus about 1220 BC. Exodus 1:11 Exodus 2:23 Exodus 4:19 [10][20][9]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never gives this king's name or the length of his reign.

Exodus says the sea covered "all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them" (14:28), and Psalm 136:15 that the LORD "overthrew Pharaoh and his host"; neither says in so many words that Pharaoh himself entered the sea or died.
Scripture gives no BC year for the Exodus.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThis page follows the person record for the king Moses faced, from the burning bush to the sea (Exodus 3–15), with the later verses that look back to him. Exodus never names him. Exodus 3:10 Exodus 14:28
